outcome.rationale: Preclinical data supports 70% editing efficiency for target mutation. Prior lentiviral GT achieved clinical efficacy in X-CGD. Base editing offers advantages: no vector insertional risk, endogenous gene regulation, no DSBs. Primary efficacy threshold (>=10% oxidase-positive granulocytes) appears achievable in majority of patients. Safety profile expected manageable with standard busulfan conditioning. Key risks: engraftment failure, insufficient editing durability, graft loss.

value.estimand: Single-arm safety assessment over 2 years post-infusion in adult X-CGD patients

group_predictions.safety_signal: Expected Grade 3-4 AEs related to busulfan conditioning (cytopenias, mucositis) and potential immune-related events. No unexpected base-editor specific toxicities anticipated based on preclinical data.

value.uncertainty: Limited clinical data for base editing in CGD; busulfan toxicity well-characterized but individual variation exists; small sample size limits rare event detection
value.rationale: Preclinical data showed favorable safety profile of ABE8e-SpRY with minimal off-target effects. Busulfan conditioning is standard but carries known risks. Phase 1/2 design allows dose/schedule optimization. Prior lentiviral GT experience informs manageable safety expectations.

analysis_trace.trial_identification: NCT06325709 is a Phase 1/2 open-label single-arm trial of base-edited autologous HSPCs for X-linked CGD (CYBB c.676C>T mutation). Sponsor: NIAID. Status: RECRUITING. Expected completion: 2032.
analysis_trace.indication: X-linked chronic granulomatous disease (X-CGD), a rare primary immunodeficiency caused by CYBB mutations affecting gp91phox and NADPH oxidase activity.
analysis_trace.patient_population: Adult males (18-75 years) with confirmed CYBB c.676C>T mutation, history of serious infections, clinically stable for conditioning. N=15 estimated.
analysis_trace.target_mechanism: ABE8e-SpRY adenine base editor corrects the C>T mutation at position c.676 in CYBB, restoring endogenous gp91phox expression without double-strand breaks. Preclinical data showed up to 70% correction efficiency in HSPCs.
analysis_trace.endpoint_interpretation: Primary-0: Safety endpoint (AEs/SAEs) over 2 years. Primary-1: Efficacy threshold >=10% oxidase-positive granulocytes at 12 months. Secondaries: gp91 expression, edited myeloid cells, DHR+ cells, infection frequency, allele stability.
analysis_trace.safety_analysis: Busulfan conditioning (12 mg/kg) carries risks of mucositis, cytopenias, infection. Immunosuppression with alemtuzumab and sirolimus adds infection risk. Base editing off-target profile appears favorable per preclinical data.
analysis_trace.key_risks: 1) Engraftment failure or poor durability; 2) Insufficient editing efficiency to reach 10% threshold; 3) Busulfan toxicity; 4) Immune response to edited cells; 5) Graft loss (observed in 3/19 prior lentiviral CGD patients).
analysis_trace.evidence_to_prediction: Preclinical study (Sci Transl Med 2024) demonstrated 70% correction efficiency for CYBB c.676C>T in HSPCs, with stable edited alleles post-transplant in mice. Prior lentiviral GT (Nat Med 2020) achieved 16-46% oxidase-positive neutrophils in 6/7 survivors at 12 months. Base editing avoids vector insertional risk and should achieve comparable or better engraftment with endogenous regulation.
analysis_trace.coverage_gaps: No published clinical results for this specific trial as of cutoff. Phase 1/2 design with small sample (n=15) limits precision. Long-term durability (>2 years) uncertain. No direct comparative data for base editing vs lentiviral GT in humans.
